about: Domaine Belargus was created in 2018 when Ivan Massonnat, a financier from the Savoie whose grandfather kept a small vineyard, bought the estate of Jo Pithon in the Layon Valley. Massonnat had fallen for Burgundy and its idea of terroir, and believes Chenin Blanc can speak of place as clearly as Pinot Noir. With winemaker Adrien Moreau and Pithon as a consultant, he has built a 24-hectare collection of crus, lieux-dits and monopoles across Anjou, Savennières and Quarts de Chaume.

“Anjou Noir” refers to western Anjou’s dark schist soils from the Armorican Massif, unlike the white limestone of Saumur to the east. This cuvée blends four parcels around Saint-Lambert-du-Lattay on black schist, puddingstone and serpentine, from vines about 30 years old. The estate is certified organic and farms biodynamically. Grapes are picked by hand, pressed directly and fermented with native yeasts, then aged about twelve months in oak vats and 400-litre French barrels.

The 2022 is subtle, pure and refreshing, with a slightly reductive bouquet of almonds, white fruit, spring flowers and orchard fruit, a medium to full body and a delicate finish. Look too for green apple, quince and lemon peel, with citrus, pear and crushed apple on the palate. It is the estate’s introduction to Anjou Noir and can age well beyond a decade.
